description:
We are a team of two building LUNA-LIFE for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, a browser simulation of a lunar outpost at the Moon’s south pole.

Abdullo Ashurov, team captain, built the project end to end: the simulation engine, the NASA data integration and the interface. His skills are JavaScript, React, Python and AI/ML.

Imomov Rajab Muhammad built the project’s demo presentation page and tested the project: he found bugs and errors and reported them to the captain to fix.

LUNA-LIFE is an interactive space exploration and simulation platform that allows users to explore the possibilities of establishing human settlements beyond Earth. It combines an animated 3D solar system with realistic planetary environments, resource management, mission planning, and settlement simulations.

Users can select a celestial body and explore its environmental conditions, available resources, construction possibilities, and estimated mission costs. The platform offers two modes: an accessible experience for general users and a Professional Mode with more detailed scientific information and simulation controls.

A key principle of LUNA-LIFE is the use of real, publicly available NASA data, including lunar topography and environmental measurements from missions such as the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO). Each scientific value is designed to include its source and instrument, while calculated results and simulation assumptions are clearly distinguished.

The project aims to make complex space science more accessible, encourage interest in planetary exploration, and help people understand the real challenges of building sustainable human settlements beyond Earth.
details:
Project Details — LUNA-LIFE

LUNA-LIFE is an interactive planetary exploration and settlement simulation platform designed to help people understand what it would take to establish sustainable human settlements beyond Earth.

The project features an animated 3D solar system where users can select different celestial bodies (excluding Earth) and explore their environments. Each destination provides an interactive experience with information about surface conditions, temperature, terrain, radiation, available resources, construction possibilities, and estimated mission costs.

LUNA-LIFE is designed with two experience modes. Explorer Mode provides a simple, visually engaging experience with minimal text, intuitive controls, and interactive planetary environments. Professional Mode offers more detailed scientific information, environmental parameters, resource assessments, and simulation tools for users interested in deeper analysis.

An essential part of the project is its commitment to real NASA data. We aim to use publicly available datasets from NASA missions and scientific archives, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), Diviner, and other relevant instruments. Scientific measurements, calculated values, and simulation assumptions are clearly distinguished. Each data value is intended to include its source, instrument, and reference link. Fictional values are only used when necessary for gameplay and are explicitly identified as simulation assumptions.

The platform is developed as a frontend application using React.js, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Python-based data preparation and analysis tools. Its architecture is designed to operate without a custom backend, using locally available datasets, static JSON files, and public NASA data sources.

What makes LUNA-LIFE creative is the combination of an interactive solar system, realistic planetary environments, resource management, and settlement planning in one accessible experience. Instead of presenting space science through long articles and static images, it allows users to explore and experiment visually.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, data transparency, accessibility, performance, realistic environmental limitations, and the distinction between real measurements and hypothetical scenarios.

Our intended impact is to make planetary science more engaging, improve public understanding of the challenges of human space exploration, and inspire students, researchers, and future explorers to think critically about humanity's future beyond Earth.
